name: Sardar Vallabh Patel International Airport
before:
Gujarat's main airport and the seventh busiest in India, handling more than 13 million passengers in the 2024 to 2025 financial year.

The two terminals are split by type rather than by airline. Terminal 1 takes domestic flights and Terminal 2, which opened to international traffic in September 2010, handles everything leaving the country. Both have 32 check in counters, and Terminal 2 has four air bridges. Clients connecting from an international arrival onto a domestic departure change buildings, so allow for it.

Air India treats the airport as a focus city and IndiGo runs an operating base here, which between them give good domestic coverage.

It is named after Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, independent India's first deputy prime minister. Room to grow is the constraint, and a new airport at Dholera is being developed for that reason.
after:
Gujarat's main airport and the seventh busiest in India, handling more than 13.8 million passengers in the 2025 to 2026 financial year.

Terminal 2 takes international flights. Since 29 March 2026, the airport says, Air India and Air India Express have used Terminal 2 for domestic flights too, and it lists IndiGo and Akasa Air at both terminals. The airport asks passengers to check their terminal with the airline before travel.

It is named after Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.

claims.note: AAI's tables for April 2025 to March 2026: Gujarat's airports carried 18,699,475 passengers, 13,822,287 of them at Ahmedabad (about three quarters); the next are Surat (1.8 million), Vadodara (1.3 million) and Rajkot (1.2 million).

claims.claim: Air India flight AI171 crashed just after take-off on 12 June 2025
claims.why: Held back: a new fact that replaces nothing in the old text, for Andy to decide on. Air India's Boeing 787 VT-ANB, flight AI171 from Ahmedabad to London Gatwick, crashed immediately after take-off on 12 June 2025 into buildings including the BJ Medical College hostel. AAIB's preliminary report counts 12 crew and 229 passengers killed, one passenger seriously injured, and 19 others killed on the ground; Wikipedia gives the same totals.
